_metadata.descripcion: Descriptores semánticos utilizados en el análisis bibliométrico-semántico del corpus de movilidad urbana.
_metadata.agregacion: Para cada descriptor se calcula la similitud coseno con cada uno de los tres modelos y se utiliza el promedio de las tres similitudes.
_metadata.nota_contacto: CONTACTO_DIRECTO, PRESENCIA_CAMPO e INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL son ejes transversales y no categorías que compitan mediante argmax con las tres orientaciones principales. PRESENCIA_CAMPO e INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL se utilizan para distinguir formas de producción empírica. El score CONTACTO_DIRECTO se conserva como indicador general de referencia, pero no se interpreta como una combinación neutral de las dos subdimensiones, debido a su mayor asociación empírica con INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL.

URBAN_MOBILITY_TRANSPORT: Research in which the substantive object of study is the physical movement, travel, accessibility, or transportation of people or goods within an urban or metropolitan context. This includes urban public transport, buses, metro, tram and rail services; private vehicle travel and urban traffic; walking, cycling and active mobility; commuting, trips and travel; passenger movement; urban freight and city logistics; transport networks, services, infrastructure, planning and operations when these are examined as components of urban mobility or transportation. The defining criterion is that urban mobility or urban transport itself constitutes a central object of the research rather than merely an incidental application context.
TECNICISTA: Urban mobility or transport approached as a system, network, infrastructure, or operation whose functioning, efficiency, performance, cost, design, prediction, control, or optimization constitutes the central research problem. This includes route and network optimization, traffic flow, congestion, scheduling and frequencies, capacity, level of service, reliability, and intelligent transportation systems; the economic evaluation of transport through operating costs, cost-benefit analysis, pricing, fares, tolls, demand modelling, generalized cost, and economic efficiency; and the instruments through which this knowledge is produced, namely mathematical and statistical modelling, econometric estimation, regression and discrete choice models, traffic and transport simulation, forecasting, algorithms, optimization procedures, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and the exploitation of large-scale digital datasets, sensor records, and big data sources.
AMBIENTAL: Environmental impacts, externalities, or consequences of urban mobility or transport, substantively measured, modelled, or evaluated. This includes greenhouse gas and CO2 emissions, air pollution and air quality, traffic noise, energy consumption, fossil fuel use, climate change, carbon footprint, decarbonization, life-cycle assessment, environmental sustainability and sustainable mobility, and ecological impacts directly attributable to transport systems and mobility practices.
SOCIAL_HUMANA: Urban mobility or transport examined in relation to people, social groups, and human experience -- combining the empirical description of social differences, inequalities, or lived mobility experiences among population groups with explicit ethical or normative reflection on the meaning, justice, dignity, care, responsibility, or human significance of mobility. This includes social exclusion, poverty, unequal accessibility, socio-spatial segregation, and differences in access to opportunities among groups defined by income, class, gender, age, disability, ethnicity, or other social positions, together with moral perception, virtue, care, hospitality, recognition, responsibility, alterity, and explicit reflection on justice, injustice, dignity, or the human meaning of movement and encounter.
CONTACTO_DIRECTO:
Empirical knowledge generated through the researcher's direct presence in
real-world mobility or transport settings or through direct interaction with
people participating in those settings. This includes manual traffic and
pedestrian counts, turning-movement counts, vehicle classification counts,
speed and travel-time measurements, delay and queue observations, parking
surveys, roadside and intersection observations, on-site audits, field
inspections, direct observation at streets, stations, stops, corridors or
transport facilities, as well as ethnographic fieldwork, interviews, focus
groups, oral histories, go-along, ride-along and walk-along methods,
participant diaries, participatory workshops, co-design, co-creation and
participatory action research. The defining feature is that empirical material
is generated through direct presence in the mobility setting or direct
engagement with people involved in mobility.
PRESENCIA_CAMPO:
Empirical data generated through direct observation or measurement in
real-world mobility or transport settings. This includes manual traffic counts,
pedestrian counts, turning-movement counts, vehicle classification counts,
spot-speed measurements, travel-time and delay studies, queue-length
observations, parking occupancy surveys, roadside and intersection
observations, on-site audits, field inspections, direct observation of
pedestrian or vehicle movements, and field-based measurements conducted at
streets, intersections, stations, stops, corridors or transport facilities.
INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL:
Empirical knowledge generated through direct interaction with people in order
to understand their situated mobility practices, experiences, perceptions,
interpretations, accounts or meanings. This includes ethnographic fieldwork
involving participants, participant observation, in-depth and semi-structured
interviews, qualitative interviews with participants or informants, focus
groups, oral histories, life-history interviews, go-along, ride-along and
walk-along methods, participant-kept diaries, photo-elicitation with
participants, participatory workshops, co-design, co-creation and
participatory action research.
